justification: Real numbers from report.json: Lighthouse 96 / 100 / 100 / 100 on the first run (no re-run needed), 0 console errors, 0 console warnings, 0 broken links, 0 px mobile overflow; the only verify failure is the expected NEEDS_MARKUS placeholder. Fresh judgement first: as a designed page this is clearly ahead of the ranking results I read. Coding Horror is a short Venn-diagram post with two four-row tables and no exercises; GeeksforGeeks is keyword-by-keyword with Venn images and screenshot outputs; W3Schools is a 600-word bullet taxonomy. None has a row-level figure, a NULL key, ON-vs-WHERE, fan-out, or a phone-legible diagram. Ours: the hook (three near-identical queries whose RESULT panels differ in one cell) is shown rather than told; nearly every query is followed at once by a terminal-style RESULT panel; the longest prose run before the final section is about seven desktop lines; headings are specific and the single h3 nests correctly in the TOC; five figures (match lines, the 4x5 truth grid, the INNER/LEFT/RIGHT/FULL bracket figure, the self-join match lines, the crossed loan/payment lines) are all informative, sit on 350-unit canvases, are legible at 390 px, put annotations under the drawing, and swap amber/green/red/accent tokens correctly in dark theme (checked desktop-dark parts 04 and 11 and every mobile-dark part). Captions say what to notice. Callouts are restrained and well chosen (two pitfalls, one .NET), three exercises are placed mid-article where they belong with collapsed solutions, and all 15 sources are now linked at the point of the claim. SQL blocks are consistently broken under ~40 columns and every RESULT panel fits a phone without clipping. Round-1 check (all three critics): every blocker/major is genuinely fixed, not papered over. Exercise 'predict' output is now inside the solution and the exercise sits after the fan-out section; the 'Exercises' ending is gone; SQL and result-panel clipping on mobile is fixed (EXISTS correlations, NOT IN subquery, owes expression, pay_id/amount result, NULL comparison result all fully visible in mobile-dark parts 11, 15, 16, 19, 20); figure numbering runs 1-5 and the 'payment_idamount' header collision is gone (now pay_id / amount with a clear gap); a self-join figure was added; the NOT IN expansion is a block inside a dedicated pitfall; the empty NOT IN result is now an explicit COUNT of 0; ANTI JOIN is scoped to the four engines with Spark cited; algorithm costs and conditions are present; MySQL/T-SQL/PostgreSQL planner sources are cited inline; RIGHT JOIN is executed; docs/crosslinks/databases/sql-joins.md exists and lists eight sensible targets with exact placement, and the page now ends with a Keep reading block, so it is no longer a dead end. What remains are nits only: the long C# program (and the two WriteLine lines in the .NET callout) still lose their last one to four characters to the fade on a phone, though only closing punctuation and never the operative part; the final section is the one place the text/figure rhythm breaks (about two and a half phone screens of dense bullets and paragraphs with costs that would scan better as a small table); the second paragraph inside the Hash join bullet renders with no gap; and Figure 2's NULL row and Figure 3's row-count labels are tight at 390 px. That is 8.5-with-nits territory and, given how far the illustration and rhythm exceed every ranking page, I put it at 8.7.
